gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Project Farm's long-term test (NiMH AA cells cycling in outdoor solar lights; a 2024 forum summary of the video says six years and about 2,200 cycles) left a Panasonic eneloop at 1,874 mAh, close to new, while other named rechargeables collapsed: Amazon Basics Silver 1 mAh, Duracell Rechargeable 259 mAh, PowerEx Pro 588 mAh.
standout_why: I opened the cited Ideal Garden Lights guide, the cited Tenergy Solla 1000 mAh product page and solarpatiolights.net (result 16). None has a measured figure. Ideal Garden Lights gives only general mAh advice and a 1-2 year replacement claim. Tenergy's page lists 2,000 cycles, -4 to 122 °F and 'up to 5 years' with no test data, and its Reviews tab is empty. Solarpatiolights gives rated mAh and its own unexplained star scores (Tenergy Solla 4.5/5, EBL 4.0/5) with no method. Adorama (result 1) returned 403. No rival gives a tester's name or a capacity measured after years of solar-light use.
decides: This supports the page's eneloop 2000 mAh row as the proven long-life choice. It is the only candidate with independent long-term data from a solar-light setting, and Stefan V's 2011 lab test also measured a 2nd-gen eneloop AA close to its rating with about 90% kept after 7 weeks. It does not rank Tenergy Solla, EBL Solar 1300, Brightown or Lightalent, because I found no independent measurement of any of them. Their '2,000 cycles' and '5 years' claims stay maker-only, and the page should say so. If you use the Project Farm numbers, credit them as 'reported from Project Farm's video'. I could not open the video's own results, and the sources disagree on details (see unsourced).

findings.label: Capacity left after long-term daily solar-light cycling (Project Farm)
findings.source_title: ResetEra: Project Farm tests a ton of batteries (alkaline/lithium/rechargeable), has list of results
findings.note: Measured by Project Farm. Video: https://youtu.be/efDTP5SEdlo. Figure taken from the thread's opening post (2024-12-15), which says 'after 6 years of daily use' (about 2,200 recharge cycles) and calls the eneloop 'essentially good as new'. SlashGear (Jack Picone, 2026-04-21) confirms that Project Farm ran rechargeables in solar lights for six years with 'Eneloop 1900' as the top NiMH. The rated minimum of 1,900 mAh would mean about 99% kept. I could not open the figures on the video itself.

findings.label: Same Project Farm long-term test: other named cells' capacity left
findings.value: IKEA LADDA 2,385 mAh; Energizer Recharge 1,931 mAh; Amazon Basics Black 1,754 mAh; EBL (standard AA, not the Solar 1300) 1,733 mAh; Thunderbolt Magnum 1,634 mAh; Rayovac Recharge 997 mAh; PowerEx Pro 588 mAh; Duracell Rechargeable 259 mAh; Amazon Basics Silver 1 mAh
findings.source_title: ResetEra: Project Farm tests a ton of batteries (alkaline/lithium/rechargeable), has list of results
findings.note: Measured by Project Farm. Values as listed in the forum post of 2024-12-15 (six years of daily use). Varta Recharge 1,960 mAh and Active Energy 1,058 mAh were run for five years only. The EBL tested is EBL's regular AA line. The EBL Solar 1300 mAh cell on our page was not in the test.

findings.label: Test setup: rechargeable AAs cycled in outdoor solar lights
findings.value: about 12 NiMH models; 'Eneloop 1900' top NiMH; Amazon Basics High-Capacity last, 'five times as poorly' as the eneloop
findings.source_title: SlashGear: Are Amazon Basics AA Batteries Better Than Costco's? These Tests Have The Answer
findings.note: SlashGear (Jack Picone, 2026-04-21) reporting Project Farm's test. It gives no mAh values. Its 'five times as poorly' ratio does not match the forum figure for Amazon Basics Black (1,754 mAh). The forum lists Silver at 1 mAh, so SlashGear may mean a different cell or measure.

findings.label: Measured capacity and charge kept after storage
findings.value: 1,893 mAh just recharged; 1,745 mAh (92.2%) after 1 week; 1,694 mAh (89.5%) after 7 weeks
findings.source_title: Stefan Vorkoetter: Review: Pre-Charged (Low Self-Discharge) Rechargeable Battery Comparison
findings.note: Tested August 2011 on a BattMan II: 1,200 mA charge and discharge, -ΔV cutoff, one cell. This is an older eneloop generation than the current 2,100-cycle cell on our page. Stefan's 6- and 12-month numbers are his own extrapolations, so I left them out.

findings.product: Tenergy Centura AA 2000 mAh (Tenergy's older low-self-discharge AA, not Solla)
findings.label: Measured capacity and charge kept after storage
findings.value: 1,950 mAh just recharged; 1,787 mAh (91.7%) after 1 week; 1,727 mAh (88.6%) after 7 weeks
findings.source_title: Stefan Vorkoetter: Review: Pre-Charged (Low Self-Discharge) Rechargeable Battery Comparison
findings.note: Tested November 2010 with the same method. This is context for the Tenergy brand only. It is not a Solla cell and should not appear in a Solla row.

unsourced: Independent measured capacity, self-discharge or long-term solar-light result for Tenergy Solla 1000 mAh or Solla Premium 1300 mAh.
